newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: NEW 50 MLN DOLLAR AFRICA INVESTMENT FUND LAUNCHED.
newsitem.headline: NEW 50 MLN DOLLAR AFRICA INVESTMENT FUND LAUNCHED.

text.p: Emerging-market fund manager Regent Pacific Group announced on Monday it would launch a $50 million Undervalued Assets Africa Fund which would be 35.4 percent weighted towards investments in mining.

Regent fund manager Joe Demby told a presentation in Botswana the fund would be registered in the Cayman Islands, primary-listed on the Dublin Stock Exchange, and had applied for dual listings on the Botswana and Kenya stock exchanges.
Approvals were expected within the next three weeks.
"The fund will seek to obtain capital growth by investing in opportunities perceived to be undervalued," Demby said.
Botswana Stock Exchange chief executive Alan Norrie said the fund would be the first hedge for the country's pula currency and as such should be welcomed by domestic investors.

In terms of the target asset portfolio, 2.5 percent of the fund -- $1.25 million (4.4 million pula) - will be invested in Botswana and 10.2 percent in Kenya. South Africa tops the list with 16 percent, followed by Zimbabwe's 12.7 percent.

The portfolio's 35.4 percent weighting towards mineral resources represents mining in Ghana, Zimbabwe, Guinea Bissau, Sierra Leone and Burkina Faso. The fund will also invest in Eqypt, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Mauritius, Morocco and Nigeria.
Demby told potential investors the fund would seek to avoid being dominated by exposure to South Africa, the characteristic of so many regional investment programmes.
"We want to invest in markets which others have not yet realised the potential of," he said.
The Regent Pacific Group is a global emerging-market fund manager. It controls assets worth more than two billion dollars and was first to enter into the Phillipines and Russia.
